Character-Level Text Prediction with a Simple RNN CSE 457 — Deep Learning Lab Project

Tiny Shakespeare → character IDs → Embedding → simple tanh RNN → Linear → softmax. We predict the next character at every position in a 100-character window, giving many supervised examples per window. This is a vanilla RNN, not an LSTM or GRU. Training uses logits with CrossEntropyLoss (which includes log-softmax internally). Generation applies softmax explicitly. Run cells in order.

Dataset and leakage prevention Source: https://github.com/karpathy/char-rnn/blob/master/data/tinyshakespeare/input.txt Download once and reuse the local file. Split contiguous raw text 80/10/10 BEFORE constructing windows. Vocabulary is learned from training text only; an UNK token handles unseen validation/test characters. No windows cross split boundaries.

class CharacterWindows(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, tokens, length):
        self.tokens, self.length = tokens, length
    def __len__(self):
        return (len(self.tokens)-1) // self.length
    def __getitem__(self, index):
        start = index * self.length
        return (self.tokens[start:start+self.length],
                self.tokens[start+1:start+self.length+1])

datasets = {k: CharacterWindows(v, CONFIG['sequence_length']) for k,v in encoded.items()}
loaders = {k: DataLoader(v, batch_size=CONFIG['batch_size'], shuffle=(k=='train'),
                        num_workers=0, pin_memory=(DEVICE.type=='cuda'))
           for k,v in datasets.items()}
print('Windows per split:', {k:len(v) for k,v in datasets.items()})
example_x, example_y = datasets['train'][0]
assert torch.equal(example_x[1:], example_y[:-1])
print('Input:', ''.join(itos[i] for i in example_x))
print('Target:', ''.join(itos[i] for i in example_y))

Model Hidden state is reset between independent windows. During generation we carry hidden state forward. Gradient clipping reduces exploding gradients. Validation loss selects the checkpoint; the test set is used only after model selection.

In [4]:
class CharRNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, embedding_dim, hidden_size):
        super().__init__()
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embedding_dim)
        self.rnn = nn.RNN(embedding_dim, hidden_size, batch_first=True, nonlinearity='tanh')
        self.dense = nn.Linear(hidden_size, vocab_size)
    def forward(self, x, hidden=None):
        states, hidden = self.rnn(self.embedding(x), hidden)
        return self.dense(states), hidden

model = CharRNN(len(itos), CONFIG['embedding_dim'], CONFIG['hidden_size']).to(DEVICE)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=CONFIG['learning_rate'])
print(model)
print('Trainable parameters:', sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()))

def run_epoch(loader, training=False):
    model.train(training)
    loss_sum = correct = count = 0
    with torch.set_grad_enabled(training):
        for x,y in loader:
            x,y = x.to(DEVICE), y.to(DEVICE)
            if training:
                optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            logits,_ = model(x)
            loss = criterion(logits.reshape(-1,len(itos)), y.reshape(-1))
            if training:
                loss.backward()
                nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0)
                optimizer.step()
            loss_sum += loss.item()*y.numel()
            correct += (logits.argmax(-1)==y).sum().item()
            count += y.numel()
    return loss_sum/count, correct/count

CharRNN(
  (embedding): Embedding(66, 64)
  (rnn): RNN(64, 128, batch_first=True)
  (dense): Linear(in_features=128, out_features=66, bias=True)
)
Trainable parameters: 37570

history = []
best_loss, stale = float('inf'), 0
started = time.time()
for epoch in range(1, CONFIG['epochs']+1):
    tick = time.time()
    train_loss, train_accuracy = run_epoch(loaders['train'], True)
    val_loss, val_accuracy = run_epoch(loaders['validation'])
    row = dict(epoch=epoch, train_loss=train_loss, train_accuracy=train_accuracy,
               val_loss=val_loss, val_accuracy=val_accuracy, seconds=time.time()-tick)
    history.append(row)
    if val_loss < best_loss:
        best_loss, stale = val_loss, 0
        torch.save({'model_state': model.state_dict(), 'config': CONFIG,
                    'vocabulary': itos, 'epoch': epoch, 'val_loss': val_loss}, OUT/'best_model.pt')
    else:
        stale += 1
    (OUT/'history.json').write_text(json.dumps(history,indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
    message = (f'Epoch {epoch:02d}/{CONFIG["epochs"]} | loss {train_loss:.4f} | '
               f'acc {train_accuracy:.2%} | val loss {val_loss:.4f} | '
               f'val acc {val_accuracy:.2%} | {row["seconds"]:.1f}s')
    print(message, flush=True)
    with (OUT/'training.log').open('a', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write(message+'\n')
    if stale >= CONFIG['patience']:
        print('Early stopping: validation loss stopped improving.')
        break
print(f'Training finished in {(time.time()-started)/60:.1f} minutes.')

Held-out evaluation Accuracy is the percentage of next characters correctly predicted under teacher forcing. It does not directly measure free-running generation quality. The baseline always predicts the most common training character, using the identical test targets.

Generate text Temperature below 1 sharpens the distribution; above 1 increases randomness. Compare spelling, dialogue formatting, repetition, and coherence in the samples. A small simple RNN is expected to learn local patterns, not reliable story meaning.

In [7]:
@torch.inference_mode()
def generate(seed='ROMEO: ', length=400, temperature=0.8, random_seed=42):
    if not seed or temperature <= 0 or length < 0:
        raise ValueError('Use a nonempty seed, positive temperature, and nonnegative length.')
    unknown = set(seed)-set(stoi)
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f'Seed contains unknown characters: {unknown}')
    model.eval()
    rng = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(random_seed)
    x = torch.tensor([[stoi[c] for c in seed]],device=DEVICE)
    logits,hidden = model(x)
    result = seed
    for _ in range(length):
        scores = logits[0,-1].clone()/temperature
        scores[0] = -float('inf')  # never emit the UNK placeholder
        token = torch.multinomial(torch.softmax(scores,dim=-1),1,generator=rng)
        result += itos[token.item()]
        logits,hidden = model(token.reshape(1,1),hidden)
    return result

samples = []
for temperature in [0.5,0.8,1.2]:
    sample = f'--- Temperature {temperature} ---\n'+generate(temperature=temperature)
    samples.append(sample)
    print(sample+'\n')
(OUT/'generated_samples.txt').write_text('\n\n'.join(samples),encoding='utf-8')

Extended visual analysis These plots use the saved best checkpoint and held-out test data, without retraining. Test diagnostics are descriptive, not used to select the model. Generated-text statistics are proxies for style and diversity, not measures of meaning or literary quality.

from pathlib import Path
import json, math
from collections import Counter
import numpy as np
import torch
from torch import nn
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch

ROOT = Path.cwd()
OUT = ROOT/'outputs'
FIG = OUT/'figures'
FIG.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.rcParams.update({'figure.dpi':110, 'axes.spines.top':False, 'axes.spines.right':False})
device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')
torch.set_num_threads(4)
saved = torch.load(OUT/'best_model.pt', map_location=device, weights_only=True)
cfg, vocab = saved['config'], saved['vocabulary']
lookup = {c:i for i,c in enumerate(vocab)}
class AnalysisRNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(len(vocab),cfg['embedding_dim'])
        self.rnn = nn.RNN(cfg['embedding_dim'],cfg['hidden_size'],batch_first=True)
        self.dense = nn.Linear(cfg['hidden_size'],len(vocab))
    def forward(self,x,h=None):
        z,h = self.rnn(self.embedding(x),h)
        return self.dense(z),h
net = AnalysisRNN().to(device)
net.load_state_dict(saved['model_state'])
net.eval()
corpus = (ROOT/'data/tiny_shakespeare.txt').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
a,b = int(len(corpus)*.8),int(len(corpus)*.9)
parts = {'Train':corpus[:a],'Validation':corpus[a:b],'Test':corpus[b:]}
hist = json.loads((OUT/'history.json').read_text())
metrics = json.loads((OUT/'metrics.json').read_text())
def label(c):
    return {' ':'space','\n':'newline','\t':'tab'}.get(c,c)
def finish(fig,name):
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(FIG/(name+'.png'),dpi=170,bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)
print('Loaded best checkpoint from epoch',saved['epoch'],'on',device)

length=cfg['sequence_length']; n=(len(tokens)-1)//length
xs=tokens[:n*length].reshape(n,length)
ys=tokens[1:n*length+1].reshape(n,length)
probs=[]
with torch.inference_mode():
    for start in range(0,n,cfg['batch_size']):
        logits,_=net(xs[start:start+cfg['batch_size']].to(device))
        probs.append(logits.softmax(-1).cpu().numpy())
p=np.concatenate(probs)
truth=ys.numpy().ravel(); prob=p.reshape(-1,len(vocab)); pred=prob.argmax(1)
correct=pred==truth; confidence=prob.max(1)
assert abs(correct.mean()-metrics['test_accuracy'])<1e-8
cm=np.zeros((len(vocab),len(vocab)),dtype=np.int64)
np.add.at(cm,(truth,pred),1)
support=cm.sum(1)
recall=np.divide(cm.diagonal(),support,out=np.zeros(len(vocab)),where=support>0)
precision=np.divide(cm.diagonal(),cm.sum(0),out=np.zeros(len(vocab)),where=cm.sum(0)>0)
print(f'Analyzed {len(truth):,} next-character predictions; test accuracy {correct.mean():.2%}.')

Analyzed 111,500 next-character predictions; test accuracy 46.68%.

  1. Temperature changes the next-character distribution All three distributions use the same seed and checkpoint. Higher temperature flattens probabilities. The 12 leading candidates are shown; other probability mass is omitted from the bars. Entropy is computed over the full vocabulary.
In [11]:
seed='ROMEO: '
with torch.inference_mode(): logits,_=net(torch.tensor([[lookup[c] for c in seed]],device=device))
scores=logits[0,-1].detach().cpu().numpy(); scores[0]=-np.inf
temperatures=[.5,.8,1.2]
distributions=[]
for temp in temperatures:
    z=scores/temp; q=np.exp(z-np.max(z)); q/=q.sum(); distributions.append(q)
leading=np.argsort(distributions[1])[-12:][::-1]
fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(13,4))
for j,(temp,q) in enumerate(zip(temperatures,distributions)):
    axes[0].bar(np.arange(12)+(j-1)*.25,q[leading],.25,label=f'T={temp}')
axes[0].set(xticks=np.arange(12),xticklabels=[label(vocab[i]) for i in leading],title=f'Next-character distribution after {seed!r}',ylabel='Probability'); axes[0].legend()
entropy=[-np.sum(q[q>0]*np.log2(q[q>0])) for q in distributions]
axes[1].plot(temperatures,entropy,'o-'); axes[1].set(title='Uncertainty vs temperature',xlabel='Temperature',ylabel='Entropy (bits)')
finish(fig,'09_temperature_distribution')
  1. Generated-text diversity and character composition Each temperature uses five fixed random seeds, producing 1,000 new characters per seed. Error bars show one standard deviation, not confidence intervals. Distinct trigrams are unique 3-character strings divided by all 3-character strings. More diversity does not necessarily mean better text. The reference uses five disjoint 1,000-character excerpts from held-out real text.
In [12]:
@torch.inference_mode()
def analysis_generate(temp,random_seed,count=1000):
    rng=torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(random_seed)
    x=torch.tensor([[lookup[c] for c in seed]],device=device)
    z,h=net(x); result=[]
    for _ in range(count):
        s=z[0,-1].clone()/temp; s[0]=-float('inf')
        token=torch.multinomial(s.softmax(-1),1,generator=rng)
        result.append(vocab[token.item()]); z,h=net(token.reshape(1,1),h)
    return ''.join(result)
def text_stats(t):
    counts=np.array(list(Counter(t).values()),dtype=float); q=counts/counts.sum()
    grams=[t[i:i+3] for i in range(len(t)-2)]
    return [-np.sum(q*np.log2(q)),len(set(grams))/len(grams),np.mean([a==b for a,b in zip(t,t[1:])])]
generated={f'T={temp}':[analysis_generate(temp,s) for s in range(5)] for temp in temperatures}
generated['Real text']=[parts['Test'][i*1000:(i+1)*1000] for i in range(5)]
fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,3,figsize=(15,4))
for j,(title,ylabel) in enumerate([('Character entropy','Bits'),('Distinct character trigrams','Ratio'),('Adjacent repeated characters','Fraction')]):
    stats=[np.array([text_stats(t) for t in texts])[:,j] for texts in generated.values()]
    axes[j].bar(list(generated),[v.mean() for v in stats],yerr=[v.std(ddof=1) for v in stats],capsize=4,color=['#3267a8','#419e75','#c47a42','#999999'])
    axes[j].set(title=title,ylabel=ylabel); axes[j].tick_params(axis='x',rotation=20)
finish(fig,'10_generated_text_diversity')
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(12,4))
for j,(name,texts) in enumerate(generated.items()):
    joined=''.join(texts); counts=Counter(joined)
    ax.bar(np.arange(len(common))+(j-1.5)*.2,[100*counts[c]/len(joined) for c in common],.2,label=name)
ax.set(xticks=np.arange(len(common)),xticklabels=[label(c) for c in common],title='Generated vs real character composition',ylabel='Frequency (%)')
ax.tick_params(axis='x',rotation=60); ax.legend()
finish(fig,'11_generated_character_distribution')

Interpretation and limitations

  • Use validation curves to discuss generalization; use test plots only for reporting.
  • The confusion matrix and per-character scores reveal which symbols are difficult.
  • Confidence and top-k plots describe next-character prediction under teacher forcing.
  • Generation is free-running and can compound errors even when test accuracy is reasonable.
  • Temperature trades predictability for diversity; read samples to assess coherence.
  • This is a single training run. Curves do not establish statistical significance.
  • ROC curves, regression residuals, and object-detection plots are not appropriate default diagnostics for this multiclass character-language-model project.
